source_text:
δόξαν δὲ πολλάκις ἡ γραφὴ λέγει αὐτὴν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν οὐσίαν· ἐπειδὴ
γὰρ ἀψηλάφητος καὶ ἀνέφικτος, δόξαν αὐτὴν ὠνόμασεν ἵνα μὴ λόγον ἀπαιτῇς ἀλλὰ
προσκυνῇς. πρῶτος τὴν οὐσίαν τοῦ θεοῦ δόξαν λέγει Ἰεζεκιὴλ ἐν ὀπτασίαις
θεασάμενος τὸν θεὸν καθεζόμενον, καὶ ἐπάγων· τοῦτο ὁμοίωμα τῆς δόξης κυρίου.
ὅπερ ἀλλαχοῦ ἑρμηνεύων ὁ θεός φησιν· ἐγὼ ὁράσεις ἐπλήθυνα 307 καὶ ἐν χερσὶ
προφητῶν ὡμοιώθην. ἣν οὖν εἶπε δόξαν ὁ Ἰεζεκιήλ, ταύτην ὁ θεός φησι τὸ ἐγώ.
λέγει δὲ Παῦλος· ὃς ὢν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης–ποίας δόξης; –καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς
ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ. κἀνταῦθα τοίνυν τὸ μὲν θεὸς τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ
κατὰ τὴν σάρκα λέγει, τὸ δὲ πατὴρ τῆς δόξης κατὰ τὴν φύσιν. Καὶ παντὸς ὀνόματος
ὀνομαζομένου οὐ μόνον ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι. ἐν γὰρ τῷ
αἰῶνι τούτῳ ὀνομάζομεν θρόνους, ἀρχάς, κυριότητας, ἐξουσίας, δυνάμεις, ἀγγέλους,
ἀρχαγγέλους· ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἔστι μυρία τάγματα ἀοράτων δυνάμεων ἡμῖν ἄγνωστα καὶ
διὰ τοῦτο ἀκατονόμαστα, μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνάστασιν ἔσται γνωστὰ καὶ λήψεται μετὰ τῆς
γνώσεως καὶ τὴν παρ' ἡμῶν προσηγορίαν, διὰ τοῦτο εἶπεν· καὶ ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι. Eph
1,22–23 Καὶ αὐτὸν ἔδωκε κεφαλὴν ὑπὲρ πάντων τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἥτις ἐστὶ τὸ σῶμα
αὐτοῦ, τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι πληρουμένου. διὰ τούτου ἐδήλωσεν ὅτι
πλήρωμα τοῦ θεοῦ λέγει τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστι τὴν ἐκκλησίαν. διὰ τί δὲ
πλήρωμα; ἐπειδὴ πεπλήρωται θεοῦ· ὥσπερ γάρ, φησίν, ἐν πᾶσι τὰ πάντα πληροῖ,
οὕτως καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ πληροῦται κατὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὴν σῶμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
Χριστοῦ οὖν σῶμα, πλήρωμα δὲ θεοῦ ἡ ἐκκλησία. Τοῦ τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι
πληρουμένου. ἔστι γὰρ ἐν οὐρανῷ, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ἐνεργῶν οὐχ ὡς ἐν γῇ, καὶ ἔστιν ἐν
γῇ, οὐχ ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ ἐνεργῶν, καὶ ἐν ἀγγέλοις, ἐν ἡλίῳ, ἀλλ' ἐν ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν
αὐτοῦ φύσιν· λέγει γὰρ ἀφ' ὧν μεταλαμβάνομεν ἡ γραφὴ περὶ θεοῦ, οὐκ ἀφ' ὧν
αὐτός ἐστιν· τοῦτο γὰρ ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστιν. Eph 2,2–3 Κόσμος διττῶς λέγεται, καὶ ἡ
σύστασις ἡ δημιουργικὴ καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸ σύστημα τὸ πονηρόν. νυνὶ δὲ διεῖλε
τοῖς ἀνόμοις τὰ πράγματα, αἰῶνα καλέσας τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὴν πονηρίαν καὶ τὴν
ἁμαρτίαν, κόσμον δὲ τὴν σύστησιν τοῦ παντός, καθὼς καὶ ἐν τῇ πρὸς Γαλάτας λέγει·
ὅπως ἐξέληται ἡμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ ἐνεστῶτος αἰῶνος πονηροῦ. τοῦτον τὸν νῦν αἰῶνα λέγει.
τὴν οὖν κοινὴν 308 ἀπόστασιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ πλάνην αἰῶνα ὠνόμασεν, ἧς
μέρος ἦσαν ποτὲ καὶ οἱ νῦν πιστεύσαντες τῷ Χριστῷ. Κατὰ τὸν ἄρχοντα τῆς ἐξουσίας
τοῦ ἀέρος τοῦ πνεύματος. φανερῶς διὰ τούτου δείκνυσιν ὁ ἀπόστολος, ὅτι οὐκ ἀπ'
οὐρανοῦ ἄγγελος ἦν ὁ διάβολος, ἀλλ' ἀέριόν τι πονηρὸν πνεῦμα. κἂν ὁ κύριος λέγῃ·
εἶδον τὸν σατανᾶν ὡς ἀστραπὴν πεσόντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, οὐχὶ τὸν τόπον δείκνυσιν
ὅθεν ἔπεσεν, ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ ἄνωθεν ἡ ἀστραπὴ ὀξέως πίπτει, τὴν ὀξύτητα τῆς
διαβολικῆς πτώσεως ἀστραπῇ παρέβαλε λέγων· ὡς ἀστραπὴ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ὀξέως
φέρεται, οὕτως εἶδον τὴν πτῶσιν αὐτοῦ ὀξεῖαν. Τοῦ νῦν ἐνεργοῦντος. ἐδήλωσεν ὅτι
οὐ πάντοτε τὴν ἰσχὺν ὁ διάβολος ἔχει, ἀλλ' ἡ ἀσθένεια τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἰσχὺς αὐτῷ
γέγονεν. Ποιοῦντες τὰ θελήματα τῆς σαρκὸς καὶ τῶν διανοιῶν. ἐκ τούτου δείκνυται
ὅτι οὐκ ἀντίκειται ἡ σὰρξ τῇ ψυχῇ· συνεφώνει γὰρ εἰς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν. Καὶ ἦμεν τέκνα
φύσει ὀργῆς. ὥσπερ υἱοὶ γεέννης, οὕτω καὶ τέκνα ὀργῆς. Eph 2,10 Ἐπειδὴ εἶπεν
κτισθέντες, λέγει· ἡ κτίσις οἰκείωσίς ἐστιν. τὸ δὲ ἐπὶ ἔργοις ἀγαθοῖς ἐπήγαγεν, ἵνα
λοιπὸν σαυτὸν οἰκοδομῇς. Eph 2,13 Οὐκ εἶπεν «ἐγγύτερον» τῶν πιστευσάντων ἀπὸ
περιτομῆς, ἀλλ' ἐγγύς. Eph 2,14–15α Τὸ μεσότοιχον τοῦ φραγμοῦ λύσας, οὐ τὸν
φραγμόν, ἀλλὰ τὸ μεσότοιχον. τίς δὲ ὁ φραγμός;
thought_title: Glory as God's essence, and the church as God's fullness
orientation: Severian is explaining Ephesians 1:17-23, first why Scripture calls God's essence 'glory,' then how the church is the body of Christ and the fullness of God, and finally the meaning of 'world' and the devil's power in Ephesians 2:2-3.
pass_a_gloss: But Scripture often calls the very essence of God 'glory'; for since it is untouchable and unattainable, it named it 'glory' so that you may not demand an account but worship. Ezekiel first calls the essence of God 'glory,' having seen in visions God seated, and adding: 'This is the likeness of the glory of the Lord.' Which elsewhere God, interpreting, says: 'I multiplied visions and in the hands of prophets I was likened.' The glory, then, which Ezekiel spoke of, this God calls 'the I.' And Paul says: 'Who being the radiance of the glory'—of what glory?—'and the exact imprint of his substance.' Here, then, 'God of our Lord Jesus Christ' he says according to the flesh, but 'Father of glory' according to nature. 'And of every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the one to come.' For in this age we name thrones, principalities, dominions, authorities, powers, angels, archangels; but since there are countless orders of invisible powers unknown to us and therefore unnameable, and after the resurrection they will be known and will receive along with the knowledge also the naming from us, therefore he said: 'and in the one to come.' Eph 1:22-23 'And him he gave as head over all things to the church, which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all things in all things.' Through this he showed that he calls the body of Christ the fullness of God, that is, the church. But why 'fullness'? Because it has been filled with God; for just as, he says, he fills all things in all things, so also in the church he is filled according to its being the body of Christ. Therefore the church is the body of Christ, but the fullness of God. 'Of him who fills all things in all things.' For he is in heaven, that is, working not as on earth, and he is on earth, not working as in heaven, and in angels, in the sun, but in each according to its nature; for Scripture speaks to us about God from the things we share in, not from the things he himself is; for this is incomprehensible. Eph 2:2-3 'World' is said in two ways: both the creative constitution and the wicked system of humans. But now he divided the matters to the lawless, calling the wickedness and sin of humans 'age,' and 'world' the constitution of the universe, just as also in the letter to the Galatians he says: 'that he might deliver us from the present evil age.' This present age he means. The common apostasy, then, and error of humans he named 'age,' of which those now believing in Christ were once a part. 'According to the ruler of the authority of the air, of the spirit.' Clearly through this the apostle shows that the devil was not an angel from heaven, but some evil aerial spirit. Even if the Lord says: 'I saw Satan falling like lightning from heaven,' he does not show the place from which he fell, but since lightning falls swiftly from above, he compared the swiftness of the devil's fall to lightning, saying: as lightning is borne swiftly from heaven, so I saw his fall swift. 'Of the one now working.' He showed that the devil does not always have the strength, but the weakness of humans has become strength for him. 'Doing the wills of the flesh and of the thoughts.' From this it is shown that the flesh is not opposed to the soul; for it agreed together into sin. 'And we were children by nature of wrath.' Just as sons of Gehenna, so also children of wrath. Eph 2:10 Since he said 'having been created,' he says: the creation is a making-one's-own. But he added 'for good works,' so that from now on you may build yourself up. Eph 2:13 He did not say 'nearer' than those who believed from circumcision, but 'near.' Eph 2:14-15a Having destroyed the dividing wall of the fence, not the fence, but the dividing wall. But what is the fence?

choices.why: Keeps the neuter subject 'Scripture' (ἡ γραφή) implicit as in the Greek, and preserves the double accusative construction with 'glory' as the name given to God's essence.

choices.term: ἵνα μὴ λόγον ἀπαιτῇς ἀλλὰ προσκυνῇς
choices.english: so that you may not demand an account but worship
choices.why: Preserves the second-person address and the sharp contrast between demanding a rational account and worshiping, which is the rhetorical point.
rejected: so that you might not ask for a word but bow down
lest you seek an explanation rather than adore

choices.why: Renders the substantivized pronoun literally, preserving Severian's point that God identifies his own being with the 'I' of the vision.

choices.term: κατὰ τὴν σάρκα ... κατὰ τὴν φύσιν
choices.english: according to the flesh ... according to nature
choices.why: Keeps the parallel prepositional phrases exactly, since the distinction between flesh and nature is the theological crux of the passage.
rejected: with respect to the flesh ... with respect to nature

choices.term: τὸ μεσότοιχον τοῦ φραγμοῦ λύσας, οὐ τὸν φραγμόν, ἀλλὰ τὸ μεσότοιχον
choices.english: Having destroyed the dividing wall of the fence, not the fence, but the dividing wall
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'dividing wall' and preserves the emphatic correction 'not the fence, but the dividing wall,' which is the whole point of Severian's distinction.
rejected: having broken down the middle wall of the partition, not the partition, but the middle wall
destroying the barrier of the hedge, not the hedge, but the barrier

choices.why: Renders the noun literally as a process of being made one's own, preserving the unusual theological term without importing 'adoption' or 'appropriation' from elsewhere.

pass_b_english: Scripture often calls God's very essence "glory." Since that essence is untouchable and unattainable, Scripture named it "glory" so that you may not demand an account but worship. Ezekiel is the first to call God's essence "glory," when in visions he saw God seated and added, "This was the likeness of the glory of the Lord" (Ezekiel 1:28). Interpreting this elsewhere, God says, "I multiplied visions and was likened through the prophets" (Hosea 12:10). So the "glory" Ezekiel spoke of is what God calls "the I." And Paul says, "He is the radiance of the glory"—of what glory?—"and the exact imprint of his substance" (Hebrews 1:3). Here, then, he calls him "God of our Lord Jesus Christ" according to the flesh, but "Father of glory" according to nature.

And every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the age to come (Ephesians 1:21). For in this age we name thrones, rulers, dominions, authorities, powers, angels, archangels. But since there are countless orders of invisible powers unknown to us and therefore unnameable, and after the resurrection they will be known and will receive their titles from us along with that knowledge, for this reason he said, "and in the age to come."

And he gave him as head over all things to the church, which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all things in all (Ephesians 1:22-23). Through this he made clear that he calls the body of Christ—that is, the church—the fullness of God. Why "fullness"? Because it has been filled with God. For just as he fills all things in all, so also he fills the church, in that it is the body of Christ. So the church is the body of Christ and the fullness of God.

Of him who fills all things in all. For he is in heaven, working in a heavenly way, and on earth, working in an earthly way, and in angels, in the sun, but in each according to its own nature. For Scripture speaks about God from the things we share in, not from what he himself is; that is incomprehensible.

"World" is used in two ways: the created order, and the wicked system of human beings. Here Paul divided the two realities, calling human wickedness and sin "age," and the constitution of the universe "world," just as he also says in Galatians: "to rescue us from the present evil age" (Galatians 1:4). He means this present age. So he named the common human rebellion and error "age," of which those who now believe in Christ were once a part.

According to the ruler of the authority of the air, the spirit now at work (Ephesians 2:2). Through this the apostle clearly shows that the devil was not an angel from heaven, but a wicked aerial spirit. Even if the Lord says, "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven" (Luke 10:18), he is not indicating the place from which he fell. Rather, since lightning falls swiftly from above, he compared the swiftness of the devil's fall to lightning, saying: as lightning rushes swiftly from heaven, so I saw his fall as swift.
Of the one now at work. He made clear that the devil does not always have his power; rather, human weakness became his power.
Doing the desires of the flesh and of the mind (Ephesians 2:3). From this it is shown that the flesh is not opposed to the soul; for it joined in agreement with sin.
And we were by nature children of wrath (Ephesians 2:3). Just as there are sons of hell, so also children of wrath.
Since he said "created," he says: creation means making something one's own possession. And he added "for good works" so that from now on you may build yourself up.
He did not say "closer" than those who believed from circumcision, but "near" (Ephesians 2:13).
Having destroyed the dividing wall of the fence, not the fence, but the dividing wall (Ephesians 2:14). What then is the fence?
notes: The source contains two marginal numerals (307, 308) that appear to be page or folio markers from the manuscript tradition; they are not part of the text and have been omitted from the gloss.

problems.source_quote: ὃς ὢν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης–ποίας δόξης; –καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ
problems.why: Severian quotes Hebrews 1:3 as Paul, but Hebrews is anonymous, not Pauline.

problems.quote: he is filled in the church
problems.source_quote: οὕτως καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ πληροῦται
problems.why: Passive 'is filled' reverses agency; God fills the church, not vice versa.
problems.fix: so also he fills the church

problems.quote: Interpreting this elsewhere, God says, "I multiplied visions, and through the prophets I was given likenesses" (Hosea 12:10)
problems.source_quote: ὅπερ ἀλλαχοῦ ἑρμηνεύων ὁ θεός φησιν· ἐγὼ ὁράσεις ἐπλήθυνα καὶ ἐν χερσὶ προφητῶν ὡμοιώθην
problems.why: ὡμοιώθην is active ('I was likened'), not passive 'I was given likenesses.' God compares himself to prophets.
problems.fix: Interpreting this elsewhere, God says, "I multiplied visions and was likened through the prophets" (Hosea 12:10)
problems.ruling: ὡμοιώθην is passive 'I was likened/compared,' not 'given likenesses'; God is the one being compared.

problems.quote: the fullness of him who fills all things in all
problems.source_quote: τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι πληρουμένου
problems.why: πληρουμένου is passive ('being filled'), not active 'who fills'; the one being filled is Christ.
problems.fix: the fullness of him who is being filled with all things in all
problems.ruling: πληρουμένου is passive participle 'being filled,' not active 'who fills'; changes theological meaning.

edits.old: Interpreting this elsewhere, God says, "I multiplied visions, and through the prophets I was given likenesses" (Hosea 12:10).
edits.new: Interpreting this elsewhere, God says, "I multiplied visions and was likened through the prophets" (Hosea 12:10).

edits.old: so also he is filled in the church, in that it is the body of Christ.
edits.new: so also he fills the church, in that it is the body of Christ.

edits.old: the fullness of him who fills all things in all
edits.new: the fullness of him who is being filled with all things in all

fixed: The citation (Hebrews 1:3) is correct as it stands; the source quotes Hebrews 1:3, and the English already includes the citation.

problems.source_quote: ἐγὼ ὁράσεις ἐπλήθυνα καὶ ἐν χερσὶ προφητῶν ὡμοιώθην
problems.why: LXX Hosea 12:10 does not match; this is Hosea 12:11 LXX / Hebrew numbering differs.

problems.quote: the fullness of him who is being filled with all things in all
problems.source_quote: τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι πληρουμένου
problems.why: Misreads participle: God fills all things, not 'being filled'; Christ/God is the one who fills.
problems.fix: the fullness of him who fills all things in all
problems.ruling: πληρουμένου is active: 'who fills all things in all,' not passive 'being filled.' Reverses agent/patient.

edits.old: Interpreting this elsewhere, God says, "I multiplied visions and was likened through the prophets" (Hosea 12:10).
edits.new: Interpreting this elsewhere, God says, "I multiplied visions and was likened through the prophets" (Hosea 12:11).

edits.old: the fullness of him who is being filled with all things in all
edits.new: the fullness of him who fills all things in all

fixed: Changed 'is being filled with all things in all' to 'fills all things in all' to match the active participle πληρουμένου.

problems.source_quote: ἐγὼ ὁράσεις ἐπλήθυνα καὶ ἐν χερσὶ προφητῶν ὡμοιώθην
problems.why: LXX Hosea 12:11 does not match; this is Hosea 12:10 in Hebrew numbering, but the Greek citation is Hosea 12:11 LXX. However, the English 'Hosea 12:11' follows Hebrew numbering where this verse is 12:10. The brief says use Hebrew Psalm numbering where they differ, but this is not a Psalm. The citation should likely be Hosea 12:10 to match standard English Bibles, or the verse numbering is confused.

edits.old: Interpreting this elsewhere, God says, "I multiplied visions and was likened through the prophets" (Hosea 12:11).
edits.new: Interpreting this elsewhere, God says, "I multiplied visions and was likened through the prophets" (Hosea 12:10).

fixed: The only confirmed problem was the scripture citation for Hosea, which has been corrected to Hosea 12:10 to match standard English Bible numbering.

problems.why: Theological status terms shift: 'improper use' vs 'grace' vs 'nature' as contrasting modes
problems.fix: Clarify these are technical terms (katachrestikos, chariti, physis)

problems.quote: God of our Lord Jesus Christ
problems.why: Different titles for same person in different sections without explanation
problems.fix: Note these are Paul's titles being analyzed

variants.text: God of our Lord Jesus Christ

problems.quote: For he is in heaven—that is, working not as he does on earth—and he is on earth, not working as he does in heaven, and in angels, in the sun, but in each according to its own nature.
problems.why: Contradictory: says God is in heaven and on earth, then 'but in each' is unclear
problems.fix: Clarify: 'he works in each according to its nature'

problems.quote: For he is in heaven—that is, working not as he does on earth—and he is on earth, not working as he does in heaven
problems.why: The sentence is self-contradictory as English; the point about different modes of presence is lost.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'He is in heaven, working in a heavenly way, and on earth, working in an earthly way.'

problems.quote: Since he said "created," he says: the creation is a making-one's-own.
problems.why: 'Making-one's-own' is not English; reads like a literal gloss of a Greek term.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'creation means making something one's own possession.'

problems.why: Hyphenated non-word; likely mistranslation or overly literal rendering of a Greek term.
problems.fix: Use 'appropriation' or 'making something one's own possession.'

problems.quote: I multiplied visions and was likened through the prophets
problems.why: Hosea 12:10 in standard translations says God used 'similitudes' or 'parables' through prophets, not 'was likened.'
problems.fix: Check LXX text; standard rendering: 'I spoke through the prophets using parables/similitudes.'

edits.old: For he is in heaven—that is, working not as he does on earth—and he is on earth, not working as he does in heaven, and in angels, in the sun, but in each according to its own nature.
edits.new: For he is in heaven, working in a heavenly way, and on earth, working in an earthly way, and in angels, in the sun, but in each according to its own nature.

edits.old: Since he said "created," he says: the creation is a making-one's-own.
edits.new: Since he said "created," he says: creation means making something one's own possession.

fixed: The glossary problems are not translation errors in the English text; the English already uses 'grace' and 'nature' correctly, and 'God of our Lord Jesus Christ' is a direct quotation from Ephesians 1:17 being analyzed by Severian.

The sentence about God's presence is not contradictory in the source; it distinguishes modes of working in different places. The English was awkward but not a mistranslation; I have clarified it while preserving the source meaning.
The phrase 'making-one's-own' is an overly literal rendering of the Greek term for appropriation; I have replaced it with natural English.
The Hosea citation is not a mistranslation; the source Greek says 'I was likened' (ὡμοιώθην), and the English correctly renders that. The suggested change would alter the source meaning.

fixed.quote: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ "God" according to the flesh
fixed.fix: him "God of our Lord Jesus Christ" according to the flesh
fixed.note: Severian says the title 'God of our Lord Jesus Christ' (Eph 1:17) applies by the flesh and 'Father of glory' by nature; English garbles this into calling God 'God'. Proposed fix doubles 'he calls' and uses brackets.
